summary: The plan frames technical scaffolding and module ownership well but leaves several load-bearing design decisions unresolved. The biggest blockers are the navigation model (tab structure, primary/secondary destinations), inconsistent deals UI direction, unspecified auth entry/exit flow, and missing interaction states/search/filter patterns across modules. Without these, implementers will either block or produce inconsistent, generic CRM mobile UX.

ratings.information_architecture: 4/10 -- it is a 4 because no navigation model is specified (tab bar vs. drawer, primary destinations, ordering, hierarchy), module landing pages exist but their grouping rationale and entry points are undefined, and the plan notes the navigation library itself is still TBD. A 10 would have a clear navigation model, primary/secondary destination list, and grouping reasoning tied to the mobile field-staff use case.
ratings.interaction_state_coverage: 4/10 -- it is a 4 because loading and empty states are named but not specified (e.g., empty-state copy and CTA actions), search/filter interactions are not detailed, login field-level states and sign-out are absent, and error states use generic placeholders like 'retry message' or 'toast/error' without content or placement. A 10 would specify every state per interactive element: loading skeleton, empty copy + CTA, error copy + retry, success feedback, disabled/invalid, and partial states.
ratings.user_flow_completeness: 4/10 -- it is a 4 because the plan lists module features but does not describe end-to-end flows with decision points (e.g., launch → session check → login → dashboard), does not define the sign-out flow, and leaves edge cases like denied location permission for clock-in, external app return after call/email/WhatsApp, and expired-session re-authentication unaddressed. A 10 would have explicit entry points, happy path with decision points, 2-3 edge cases per flow, and exit points.
ratings.responsive_accessibility: 6/10 -- it is a 6 because React Native is mobile-first by default, but there is no mention of touch-target sizes, screen-reader labels, dynamic type/font scaling, orientation/tablet handling, or reduced-motion preferences. A 10 would explicitly state accessibility requirements (screen reader, minimum 44dp touch targets, keyboard handling where relevant) and responsive strategy.
ratings.unresolved_design_decisions: 3/10 -- it is a 3 because multiple critical interactions are described as vague alternatives ('horizontal swipe between stage columns or a list with stage filter', 'insights widget equivalent inline or as cards', 'search/filter at top', 'optional GPS if backend supports'), navigation library is deferred, and there are no mock flows or wireframe decisions for the most complex screen (deals pipeline). A 10 would resolve every interaction to a single approach with enough detail to implement without asking 'how should this work?'

ai_slop_check.assessment: The plan is not itself an AI slop artifact (no purple gradients, feature grids, or stock-photo heroes). However, the dashboard module is at risk of becoming generic SaaS KPI cards if not grounded in the field-staff persona. The plan does not explain why each KPI matters on a phone, what order supports a rep standing in front of a customer, or how the layout differs from the web dashboard. Similarly, 'recent/upcoming activities' could become a generic list without time-context, prioritization, or actionable next-step affordances.

findings.title: Navigation model and primary destination structure are entirely undefined
findings.evidence: The plan lists files such as `apps/mobile/app/(app)/index.tsx`, `deals/index.tsx`, `contacts/index.tsx`, `activities/index.tsx`, `invoices/index.tsx`, and `hr/index.tsx` but never specifies whether these are tabs in a bottom tab bar, items in a drawer, stack destinations, or a combination. The 'Open Questions' section explicitly says 'Final navigation library choice (React Navigation vs Expo Router) after spike.'
findings.suggested_fix: Add a navigation model section: bottom tab bar primary destinations (e.g., Dashboard, Deals, Contacts, Activities, More) with icon/label rationale, which modules live under a 'More' overflow, and which screens are pushed modally vs. stacked. Decide before U4/U5 so component and file output structure align.

findings.title: Deals module UI pattern is unresolved and mutually exclusive options are left open
findings.evidence: U6 Approach says: 'Render deals grouped by stage; support horizontal swipe between stage columns or a list with stage filter.' These two interaction models require different components, data layout, and gesture handling. The file list only creates `deal-card.tsx` and `deal-stage-picker.tsx` with no decision on which pattern to use.
findings.suggested_fix: Pick one pattern based on mobile context. For a field rep checking pipeline on a phone, a list with a stage filter is usually more usable than horizontal Kanban columns; for tablet/internal managers, a swipeable board might make sense. Document the chosen pattern, stage-filter placement, and deal-card actions.

findings.title: Auth entry and exit flows are underspecified
findings.evidence: U3 describes login success and token storage, but does not specify: splash/launch screen while session is checked, what happens when the app returns from background with an expired token, the sign-out entry point (profile tab? settings? account menu?), sign-out confirmation, or token wipe visual feedback. No sign-out files are created.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a user-flow section for authentication covering: app launch → session validation → (auto-login | login screen), login field validation/error display, session expiry on foreground, and sign-out trigger → confirmation → token deletion → redirect to login. Add files for launch/splash screen and settings/profile screen containing sign-out.

findings.title: Empty, error, and success states lack content and placement
findings.evidence: U5 mentions 'empty states render with CTA buttons' without specifying the CTA label, target screen, or illustration/copy. U5 error path says 'query error shows a retry message' without copy. U6 says 'mutation failure shows toast/error' but no toast placement, copy, or retry action. U9 says 'no invoices shows empty state with CTA' without content.
findings.suggested_fix: For each module, define empty-state headline, body, primary/secondary CTA labels, and target navigation. Define error-state copy, retry button label, and whether errors are inline, full-screen, or snackbar. Define success feedback for mutations (e.g., stage changed, reminder sent, clock-in recorded).

findings.title: Search and filter interactions are not designed
findings.evidence: U7 says 'Add search/filter at top' for contacts/companies. U9 says 'filter by status (outstanding, overdue, paid)' for invoices. U6 says 'list with stage filter' as an option. None specify: real-time vs. submit-based search, filter control type (chips, dropdown, segmented control), empty search results state, clear/reset behavior, or active-filter affordance.
findings.suggested_fix: Design a single search/filter pattern reusable across modules: e.g., a sticky search bar with debounced real-time filtering on contacts, and segmented chips for invoice status. Document empty-search copy, clear action placement, and whether search is local-only or query-backed.

findings.title: Dashboard KPI card layout and priority are not mobile-specific
findings.evidence: U5 Approach says: 'Render KPI cards as tappable cards (link to related module) in a scrollable vertical list' and 'Render InsightsWidget equivalent inline or as cards.' It does not say which KPIs appear above the fold, which can collapse, or how the mobile dashboard differs from the web dashboard for a field user.
findings.suggested_fix: Define the exact KPI set and order for mobile, rationale for each (e.g., 'Open deals' first because reps check pipeline before meetings), and rules for truncation/hiding on small screens. Decide whether insights are a separate card group or inline.

findings.title: Contact/company quick-action exposure is incomplete
findings.evidence: U7 says 'Detail screen shows phone, email, WhatsApp, and company link with Linking.openURL actions.' It does not specify whether these are icon buttons, text rows, a bottom action sheet, or what happens when a capability is unavailable (no WhatsApp installed, no email client).
findings.suggested_fix: Design the detail-screen action surface (e.g., persistent bottom bar with call/message/email icons, each disabled/hidden when data is missing). Add an error/feedback state when the device cannot open a URL and document whether actions are available from the list row or only from detail.

findings.title: Activities 'new' flow misses entity-linking design
findings.evidence: U8 Approach describes a 'New activity' screen with 'type picker, title, due date, linked entity.' It does not explain how the user selects the linked entity (deal, contact, company) — search picker, recent list, pre-filled from context? — nor what validation messaging looks like.
findings.suggested_fix: Design the entity-linking picker: searchable list of recent deals/contacts/companies, support for pre-fill when entering from a deal/contact detail screen, empty/unlinkable state, and required-field validation copy.

findings.title: HR clock-in flow lacks permission and offline-state handling
findings.evidence: U10 Approach says 'add a Clock In/Out button that uses device time/location (optional GPS if backend supports).' It does not specify the user flow for GPS permission denial, location fetch failure, or clock-in when the device time differs from server time. Also no design for how today's attendance summary is summarized.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a clock-in/clock-out flow: button states (clock in / clock out / already clocked), GPS permission request/denial UI, loading state during mutation, success confirmation, and error state when location/time validation fails.

findings.title: Accessibility and touch-target basics are absent
findings.evidence: No mention of screen-reader labels, minimum touch-target sizes, focus order, dynamic-type scaling, or reduced-motion support anywhere in the document.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a short design constraint section: all tappable elements minimum 44x44dp (or 48dp), screen-reader labels for icon-only buttons, respect system font scaling, and avoid auto-playing animations.

findings.title: AI slop risk: dashboard may become generic SaaS cards
findings.evidence: U5 describes 'KPI cards' and 'recent/upcoming activities' without product-specific reasoning. Without explicit prioritization for a mobile field user, the screen can default to a generic grid of four equal cards plus a chronological list.
findings.suggested_fix: Ground the dashboard in the field-staff job-to-be-done: lead with 'what needs my attention now' (overdue activities, overdue invoices), then 'quick wins' (deals moving this week), then less urgent metrics. Document why each element exists for a mobile rep.

findings.title: No mention of orientation, tablet, or responsive layout strategy
findings.evidence: React Native layout is assumed to be mobile portrait only. The plan does not say whether landscape or tablet layouts are supported, whether the app is portrait-locked, or how the UI adapts to wider screens.
findings.suggested_fix: State explicitly: portrait-only Phase 1, no tablet optimization, or document a simple breakpoint strategy (single-column on phones, two-column dashboard on tablets).
